comments.body: Do you actually have an application that emits non-ASCII header fields and needs this? Before this could be landed, we'd presumably also need to modify svix-play to handle non-ASCII header values...

No, I don't have an application of my own that emits non-ASCII response headers; I found this reading `format_resp_headers`, where `HeaderValue::to_str()?` makes `process_response` return early, so the sender never gets a response for that message. Any local server that sends obs-text bytes (e.g. a UTF-8 or Latin-1 `Content-Disposition` filename) triggers it, and the failure is only a stderr line, so it is easy to miss.

On svix-play: the CLI sends headers as a `HashMap<String, String>` in JSON, and after this change the values are always valid UTF-8 strings (invalid bytes become U+FFFD), so the wire format doesn't change. I haven't looked at how svix-play renders them, so I can't say whether it needs a change; if you'd rather not land this without that being checked, I'm happy to leave it until then or close it, whichever you prefer.

This reply was prepared with assistance from an AI coding assistant (Claude Code).
